The manipulation of time in the story is very effective and well-balanced. The writer uses the "stretching of time" for the immediate present, slowing down the pacing to focus on minute sensory details—the sticking door, the three notches under the banister, the dried lemon, and the rattling windowpane. This stretches a few minutes of real-time arrival into a deeply atmospheric exploration of grief, hesitation, and estrangement. Conversely, the writer uses "compression of time" to handle the backstory, condensing twenty years of absence, the mother's solitary final years, and her death into just a few brief, understated sentences. This contrast keeps the narrative grounded in the quiet weight of the present moment while still providing all the necessary emotional context.
